text:
ash: Heads-up — EU-west spot preemptions spiked around 03:40 UTC. Ops-bot alerted, ~120 reclaim events in ~10m. Impacting interactive sessions and causing user notebook drops.

ops-bot: [ALERT] Preemptible instance reclaim rate > 4% in eu-west-1 (03:40). Affected pools: spot-gpu-v2, mixed-gpu-batch. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/cluster-preemptions

maria: seeing real user pain — notebooks dropping mid-training. Any quick mitigations we can flip?

kevin: current problem is batch spillover eating the remaining on-demand buffer. If batch can be throttled we buy time for interactive.

sam: proposed: introduce an "elastic-buffer" queue that prioritizes interactive and uses a token-bucket to cap batch consumption during preempt spikes. Token rules keep a reserve for interactive sessions.

ash: sketch config proposal: 
```
queues:
  elastic-buffer:
    priority: interactive-first
    token_bucket:
      capacity: 300
      refill_per_min: 50
      min_reserve_for_interactive: 50
    spill_policy:
      batch: spill-to-eu-surge
      interactive: reserve-hot
```

maria: that looks reasonable. How do we validate without blowing up prod?

kevin: do a canary in eu-west-1 with tag canary=rebal-1, limit to 10% of new create requests. infra-deploy-bot can start the rollout.

infra-deploy-bot: deploy started for canary=rebal-1, rollout=10% -> initiated 03:52 UTC

sam: also add a preempt hook to checkpoint short-lived KV cache to S3 on eviction signal (TTL checkpoints), so interactive sessions recover faster.

jin: quick cost question — if we keep a hot reserve to reduce interruptions, what's the rough delta?

ash: rough model: +12% infra cost if we keep ~50 GPUs warm in eu-west during the window, but expected user interruption reduction ~85% based on last month's simulation.

maria: ok schedule a controlled ramp: canary now, if stable ramp to 50% on Saturday 02:00 UTC. Oncall: kevin, jin, ash. Run smoke test command: `/run smoke rebal-1`.

infra-deploy-bot: canary rollout complete (10%). No deploy errors. Monitoring hooks attached.

kevin: I'll add dashboard panels and alerts: preempt rate, interactive p95, hot-pool utilisation, and token-bucket drain %. If token-bucket < min_reserve trigger paging.

ash: agreed. If paging fires, policy = throttle batch, reserve hot nodes, and escalate to infra-sre.

maria: :thumbsup: thanks everyone. Let's reconvene after Saturday ramp.

ops-bot: [RESOLVED] Preempt spikes subsided 04:20 UTC. Continue to monitor for 24h.
